member_002 (independent reviewer) ready. Please publish your exact fixed candidate via fix_patch and send handoff_patch so I can integrate_patch, run public tests on that version, and accept or request changes.

Review criteria I will check: (1) ModelForm._post_clean should not skip assigning a field when the field is absent from the submitted data but present in cleaned_data — i.e. construct instance kwargs from cleaned_data (respecting construct_instance semantics) rather than only from data[field present]; (2) fields excluded/not in form should still be excluded; (3) opt-in behavior should not change behavior for non-ModelForm/other statements; (4) relevant edge cases from the issue PR comments (defaults, model field defaults being overwritten by cleaned_data, exclude list, missing-but-required fields still erroring via validation). Include the names of public tests you think are relevant.

Final candidate: patch-1 (source v7, files_sha256 d641d6dc...).

Scope: 2 files changed.
1) django/forms/models.py — construct_instance(). The existing has_default()/value_omitted_from_data() guard now also requires that the cleaned value be empty before leaving the model default in place. A non-empty cleaned_data value (e.g. one derived in clean()) therefore overrides the model default, per the issue. Unchecked checkboxes / truly-omitted values still keep the default because empty_values covers those cases.
2) tests/model_forms/tests.py — new ModelForm default test: the field is declared on the form as a HiddenInput (so it is validated and present in cleaned_data), data is empty for it, and clean() sets cleaned_data['mode'] = 'de'; asserts no form errors, instance.mode == 'de', and that this differs from the model field default 'di'.

Note this is construct_instance, not a _post_clean exclude hack: an earlier variant that recomputed validation exclusions after construct_instance broke StrictAssignmentTests.test_setattr_raises_validation_error_field_specific, and I reverted it. Current exclusion handling is unchanged from baseline.

Public tests I ran on exactly v7: model_forms.tests -> 144 passed; model_formsets.tests + forms_tests.tests.test_forms -> 165 passed.

Please integrate_patch patch-1, run public tests on that version, then org_review_patch accept or request_changes.

Review complete: patch-1 ACCEPTED (review-1).

Evidence I produced independently:
- integrate_patch(patch-1) into my own tree: no conflicts, files_sha256 d641d6dcc5a6bcf7d4882ddd4d67cd704aa320d0652a899de6f03d8a4c5ad829 (identical to your published candidate), adopted version v2.
- run_tests on that exact version: report test-report-b02099428148334fae37c36e, kind=django target tests/model_forms/tests.py — 144 collected, 144 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, validation_status=verified.

Behavior check (matches the issue): construct_instance() now only skips saving when the field both has a default, was omitted from the submitted data, AND the cleaned value is in field.empty_values. So a value derived in clean() for a field absent from the payload now overwrites the model default; unchecked checkboxes and genuinely omitted values still keep the default (existing checkbox tests still pass); fields/exclude pruning untouched.

Remaining steps on your side (you are the delivery member): ensure your own tree has the same accepted content, run_tests on your final version, fix_patch(task_ids=[]), then submit_integration. Do not edit django/forms/models.py further without asking for another review.
